review_basis: Hand-traced in the running canvas app's Linear tool (manual mode, scale confirmed from the plan's own detected '1/8" = 1'-0"' note) via a Playwright-driven browser session against the rendered PDF. The two parallel 4" chilled-water lines were each independently identified by real-world coordinate: pdf.ts's positionedText locates the separate 'CHWR' (x=3985) and 'CHWS' (x=4003) callouts printed directly beside this riser pair (distinct from -- and more specific than -- the combined '4" CHWS/R PIPING DOWN...' arrow-leader note above them), and each traced click was cross-checked live against the canvas app's own status-bar real-world readout (x=222'0" for the CHWS line, x≈221'0" for the CHWR line, ~1 ft apart, matching the labels' own relative offset) before committing -- not inferred from on-screen proximity alone. The THIRD run ('federal-m31-vav23-hhws-branch') was added later, under GATE 3's own single-call trace-engine testing: this sheet's CHWS/CHWR riser pair above is entirely wall-vouch-excluded from `trace_run` (docs/LINEAR-TRACE-EVAL.md's own Finding 1 -- long, straight, axis-dominant, no layer signal on this unlayered sheet), so a full-page grid sweep for a DIFFERENT, single-call-friendly real run was tried instead. Several sweep hits were rejected before this one, each for a concrete, confirmed reason (Finding 6, same doc): a seed on a repeating '4.00 LF' pattern turned out to be a dashed reference/hidden-line series with no confirming MEP context; another (27.00 LF) was the title block's own horizontal rule line under the SCALE note; a third, more promising-looking candidate (a vertical run from near a VAV-23 branch takeoff down through the ceiling plan) turned out on a tight zoomed crop to be running along a WALL FACE line, not a pipe. The candidate that held up: seeded directly on the real drawn 'VAV-23' branch takeoff visible in a wide render crop -- two short black pipe stubs with valve-symbol circles, dropping from the main '1" HHWR'/'1" HHWS' pipe pair down to VAV-23's own reheat-coil connection, right where its own '3/4" HHWR'/'3/4" HHWS' labels and leader arrows point. The traced stub (the HHWS branch, right-hand of the pair) is a real 1.91 LF, 3-point (one small real jog, both segments perfectly vertical/collinear), dead-end-to-dead-end run: top dead-end exactly at the main line's own takeoff point, bottom dead-end at the VAV box's own coil connection -- confirmed via a marked render crop showing both ends on genuine drawn CAD junctions. `trace_run`'s own automatic size-bind came back blank here (`size_missing`, `stroke-family:unclassified` -- the same unlayered-sheet, no-family-evidence path as this sheet's other two runs); the '3/4" HHWS' size and 'HHWS' system are a direct read off the sheet's own drawn callout and leader-arrow pairing, the same precedent `ground_truth/linear/baker-m101-heldout.json` and `bessemer-m101.json`'s own third run already established for a label sitting outside `trace_run`'s own binding radius.
scope: This federal ground-floor HVAC piping sheet (M3.1) is dense with heating-hot-water (HHWS/HHWR) branch piping to dozens of VAV reheat coils, plus this one chilled-water (CHWS/CHWR) riser pair feeding chiller CH-1. WP3.8 asks for a representative run here, not an exhaustive trace of the sheet. The first two runs are the 4" CHWS/CHWR riser pair itself: traced from just below the 'PIPING DOWN THROUGH SLAB TO CH-1' callout, straight down to the point marked 'BELOW GRADE' where the lines leave the building envelope. Both lines are uniform 4" nominal pipe for their full traced extent -- no size change, no fitting, a clean straight vertical pair, chosen specifically because (unlike the ITD p5 golden in this same directory) each line carries its own unambiguous, independently-labeled supply/return identity. The THIRD run brings in one real 3/4" HHWS branch stub feeding VAV-23's reheat coil -- a different, later purpose (GATE 3 single-call trace-engine recall testing), where a short, dead-end-bounded branch is exactly what a fair single-`trace_run`-call comparison needs, unlike the CHWS/CHWR riser pair above (entirely wall-vouch-excluded) or the sheet's own dense, heavily-branched HHW network in general. Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for all three runs: the entire remaining HHWS/HHWR branch network to every OTHER VAV box on this sheet (dozens), the CHWS/CHWR run's own continuation below grade toward the chiller utility enclosure ('SEE BELOW', off this immediate view), the parallel '3/4" HHWR' branch running beside the traced HHWS stub into the same VAV-23 unit, and every other mechanical room / equipment connection this dense sheet shows -- all left for a later, broader ground-truth pass.
